claim: Larvae of the ascidian Ciona initiate metamorphosis tens of minutes after adhesion to a substratum via their adhesive organ.
source_text: Larvae of the ascidian Ciona initiate metamorphosis tens of minutes after adhesion to a substratum via their adhesive organ.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established knowledge about Ciona metamorphosis timing and is supported by citations in the manuscript (e.g., Matsunobu and Sasakura, 2015).

claim: The gap between adhesion and metamorphosis initiation is suggested to ensure the rigidity of adhesion, allowing Ciona to maintain settlement after losing locomotive activity through metamorphosis.
source_text: The gap between adhesion and metamorphosis initiation is suggested to ensure the rigidity of adhesion, allowing Ciona to maintain settlement after losing locomotive activity through metamorphosis.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretive statement about the functional significance of the timing gap, based on logical inference from biological requirements.

claim: The gap represents the time required for sufficient cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) accumulation to trigger metamorphosis.
source_text: we propose that the gap represents the time required for sufficient cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) accumulation to trigger metamorphosis.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their experimental data from gene functional analyses, pharmacological analyses, and live imaging.

claim: The Gs pathway, Gi pathway, and Gq pathway are involved in the initiation of metamorphosis in the downstream signaling cascade of GABA.
source_text: Not only the Gs pathway but also the Gi and Gq pathways are involved in the initiation of metamorphosis in the downstream signaling cascade of the neurotransmitter GABA
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from knockdown experiments and functional analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: GABA is the known initiator of Ciona metamorphosis.
source_text: the neurotransmitter GABA, the known initiator of Ciona metamorphosis
evidence_reasoning: This refers to previously established knowledge from prior studies, specifically cited as Hozumi et al., 2020.

claim: The mutual crosstalk of stimulatory and inhibitory G-proteins functions as the accelerator and brake for cAMP production.
source_text: The mutual crosstalk of stimulatory and inhibitory G-proteins functions as the accelerator and brake for cAMP production
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretive conclusion based on the experimental data showing both stimulatory and inhibitory pathways affecting cAMP levels.

claim: Metamorphosis allows animals to have different functions between larval and adult stages.
source_text: Metamorphosis is a widespread feature of development that allows animals to have different functions between larval and adult stages
evidence_reasoning: This is established biological knowledge supported by the citation to Barresi and Gilbert, 2020.

claim: The biphasic mode of life is a widely conserved and ancient trait of animals.
source_text: This biphasic mode of life is a widely conserved and ancient trait of animals, as evidenced by its presence in groups that maintain primitive states
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citation to Arenas-Mena, 2010 and represents established evolutionary knowledge.

claim: Sufficiently matured larvae start metamorphosis only when they meet an appropriate external condition to be adults.
source_text: Sufficiently matured (or metamorphically competent Hadfield et al., 2001) larvae start metamorphosis only when they meet an appropriate external condition to be adults.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about metamorphosis competence, supported by citation to Hadfield et al., 2001.

claim: Ascidians are marine invertebrate chordates that are the closest living relatives to vertebrates.
source_text: Ascidians are marine invertebrate chordates that are the closest living relatives to vertebrates
evidence_reasoning: This is established phylogenetic knowledge supported by multiple citations (Delsuc et al., 2006; Satoh, 2003; Bourlat et al., 2006; Delsuc et al., 2008).

claim: Ascidian larvae swim by beating their tail through neuromuscular activities.
source_text: Like vertebrate tadpoles, ascidian larvae swim by beating their tail through neuromuscular activities
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about ascidian larval locomotion, supported by citations to Nishino et al., 2011 and Horie et al., 2010.

claim: Ascidians exhibit a sessile lifestyle at the adult stage.
source_text: ascidians lose the tadpole shape during metamorphosis, and they exhibit a sessile lifestyle at the adult stage
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about ascidian life history, supported by citations to Karaiskou et al., 2015 and Hotta et al., 2020.

claim: Adhesion to a substratum triggers ascidian metamorphosis.
source_text: Adhesion to a substratum triggers ascidian metamorphosis
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Cloney, 1982.

claim: Adhesive papillae secrete a lectin-type mucus substance that is suspected to aid in binding to the substratum.
source_text: Adhesive papillae secrete a lectin-type mucus substance that is suspected to aid in binding to the substratum

claim: Adhesive papillae serve as mechanical sensors.
source_text: Moreover, adhesive papillae serve as mechanical sensors

claim: The mechanical stimulus can trigger metamorphosis without a chemical stimulus under laboratory conditions.

claim: The papilla neurons (PNs) are responsible for initiating metamorphosis.

claim: A TRP channel is involved in the responsiveness to mechanical stimuli.

claim: Continuous adhesion for about 30 min is necessary before starting metamorphosis in Ciona.

claim: The strength of force generated by swimming activity influences the timing of metamorphosis initiation.

claim: The abolishment of swimming activity elongates the time from settlement until metamorphosis is initiated.
source_text: the abolishment of swimming activity elongates the time from settlement until metamorphosis is initiated

claim: GABA plays a pivotal role in initiating Ciona metamorphosis.

claim: GABA administration induces metamorphosis without adhesion.

claim: GABABR is a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR).

claim: Trimeric G-proteins are heterotrimers of an α, β, and γ subunit.

source_text: Upon ligand binding, GPCR exchanges GDP of the α subunit to GTP

claim: Gαs and Gαi, respectively, activate and inhibit cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) synthesis.
source_text: Gαs and Gαi, respectively, activate and inhibit cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) synthesis.

source_text: A previous study (Prasobh and Manoj, 2009) identified ten genes encoding Gα proteins from the Ciona genome

source_text: Gαs MO exhibited almost complete perturbation of metamorphosis, while the effect of Gαq MO was milder

source_text: Gαq activates phospholipase C beta (PLCβ) to produce inositol triphosphate (IP3)

claim: Gαq initiates metamorphosis by the conventional Ca2+ pathway mediated by PLCβ and IP3/IP3R.

claim: Most theophylline-treated larvae completed tail regression without adhesion.

claim: cAMP accumulation does not alter the timing of acquiring metamorphic competence.

claim: The genes encoding Gq and Gs pathway proteins are expressed in the adhesive papilla region.

claim: When the papillae were removed from larvae, the average rate of metamorphosis induction by theophylline was reduced from 100% to 30%.
